question.text: If a line intercepted between the coordinate axes is trisected at a point $\mathrm{A}(4,3)$, which is nearer to $x$-axis, then its equation is:

solution.text: $$ \text { A divides } \mathrm{CB} \text { in } 2: 1 $$ $$ \begin{aligned} &\Rightarrow 4=\left(\frac{1 \times 0+2 \times a}{1+2}\right)=\frac{2 a}{3} \\ &\Rightarrow a=6 \Rightarrow \text { coordinate of B is B }(6,0) \\ &3=\left(\frac{1 \times b+2 \times 0}{1+2}\right)=\frac{b}{3} \\ &\Rightarrow b=9 \text { and } \mathrm{C}(0,9) \end{aligned} $$ Slope of line passing through $(6,0),(0,9)$ slope, $m=\frac{9}{-6}=-\frac{3}{2}$ Equation of line $y-0=\frac{-3}{2}(x-6)$ $$ \begin{aligned} &2 y=-3 x+18 \\ &3 x+2 y=18 \end{aligned} $$
